Conventions
Following are the conventions used in the table headers of this document:
 Type of Request: Defines the type of request i.e. GET, PUT, POST, DELETE etc.
 Endpoint: Endpoint mentioned as '/arconToken' must be used after the hosted URL, Hosted URL will be
like, i.e 'http://www.pamapi.arconnet.com/arconToken' or 'https://www.pamapi.arconnet.com/arconToken'
or 'http://10.10.0.1:1234/arconToken'.
 Available in API Version: This refers to the API Version in which this particular Endpoint is available. i.e.
'1.0', '2.0' etc
 Release Version: This refers to which PAM release version this API was available in. i.e 'U3', 'U4', etc
 Pre Endpoint Call: Endpoints mentioned here are, per-requisites for consuming the mentioned
endpoint.
 Request: 'Params', 'Headers' & 'Body' qualifies as the 'Request', mentioned parameters in 'Request'
need to be present in while calling the API Endpoint.
 Params: These parameters, generally are a part of URL or appended to the URL.
 Headers: There can be multiple headers involved while requesting the API Endpoint. i.e 'Content-
Type', 'Accept-Header', 'x-PAM-Version' etc. In case a parameter is mentioned as 'Mandatory'
then it means that particular parameter is required for the API endpoint to respond correctly.
 Body: Body can vary, and depending on the type of request might not be a part of 'Request'.
 Response: Usually in an JSON Format. Response varies but the 'Result' part of the response varies rest
is almost always the same.
 Response Time: This is an approximate estimated response time, usually in an internal network.
 Post Endpoint Call: Endpoints mentioned here require a per-requisite of mentioned endpoint.
 Supported Features: All internal or external applications are to be mentioned here, which are currently
consuming this endpoint.

1 ActivityLogs
Before consuming APIs in the ActivityLogs section, a JWT Token must be generated and passed in the header
for all API’s given below.
1.1 GetAccessControlLogs
This API is used to fetch access control logs from ARCON PAM.
Type of Request POST
Endpoint /api/ActivityLogs/GetAccessControlLogs
Available in API
Version
All versions
Release Version U4

2. For Java using OK HTTP: https://square.github.io/okhttp/
3. For Python
a. Using HTTP client: https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.client.html
b. Using requests: https://pypi.org/project/requests/
ARCON does not take any responsibility for any bugs/vulnerabilities in the third-party libraries
neither does ARCON recommend usage for these third-party libraries. Similar code can be done in
native languages respectively for achieving the same results.

12 DeviceOnboarding
DeviceOnboarding is also an alias for Provisioning API.
Provisioning API is used to create User IDs on the server. Any third party application will communicate to
ARCON PAM API which will communicate to Provisioning API. This API can provision IDs on Servers of type
Windows RDP, SSH Linux, HP- UX, AIX, Oracle, and MS SQL.

12.3.1 Data Types of Request and Response
Type Parameters Data Type Description
Request ServerIP string This value refers to the Target server IP address
where User to be created
ServerHostname string This value refers to the Target Server hostname
where you want to create a new user
ServerDomainnam
e
string This value refers to the Target Domain name
where you want to create a User.
HostUserGroup string This value refers to the Name of group(local
group) present on target in which user should be
added after creation (for windows)
You can specify more than one group separated
by ' | ' i.e pipe symbol.
OSorDB string This value refers to the Target server type
whether Operating system or Database.
Do not pass the domain name value if
it’s a local user.
Values will be like:
 OS (for the operating system)
 DB (For the database)

## [p253]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 253

NameOfOSorDB string This value refers to the Name of the target server
type
InstanceName string This value refers to the Name of the database
instance where you want to create a user
DBName string This value refers to the Database name for the
target device
UserToBeCreated string This value refers to the Username to be created
on the target server
DBRole string This value refers to the access or privileges for
user-created on target.
Values will be like:
Windows/Linux/Unix/Solaris/Oracle/
SQL/MYSQL/ActiveDirectory
Use ActiveDirectory when creating
Domain User (Available from ARCON
PAM Ver 4.8.5.0 U18)

SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE or
ALL
Values will be comma seperated.
Available from 4850 U10.

to be created in ARCON PAM or Not.

in case don't want to create a user in the default
home directory.
Port string This value refers to the Port number for Target
Server (Will use default port if not sent)
ARCOSLOB string This value refers to the LOB ID defined in ARCON
PAM to Map the newly created service. (Use
GetLobList API to get the List of LOB in ARCON
PAM and Pass LOB ID)
ARCOSServerGrou
p
string This value refers to the Server Group ID defined
in ARCON PAM to Map the newly created service
(Use GetServerGroupList API to get the list of
Server Group Mapped to LOB ID in ARCON PAM
and Pass ServerGroup ID).
UniqueId string Currently not implemented
PrivilegedIDDomai
nName
string
Values will be like:
 "Y" - To create service in ARCON
PAM
 "N" - Not to create service in
ARCON PAM
This value will be set to ‘N' in case of
domain user creation.
To create service in ARCON PAM Use
API 'AssignGroup' in case of Domain user
creation.

e

(Currently not implemented)
IsSafe bool (Online / Offline)
In-case of Online (true) - ARCON PAM will
manage password.
In Case of Offline (false) - ARCON PAM Will not
manage password, it will only create service.
Script string This value refers to the Script for user role on the
server (In Case of SSH)
EmailId string If Requester doesn't want to send an email on
OLM ID then he has to mention the email id here.
This will be used when the ARCOSFlag parameter
is passed as "N"(means service not to be created
in ARCON PAM)
MapAllAssignedSer
viceGroups
bool This value defines whether to map service to all
server group assigned to requester user-id

## [p256]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 256
Type Parameters Data Type Description
IsCreateArcosServ
erGroup
bool Value : True - If you want to create a new Server
Group In ARCON               PAM with this request if
not present.
             False - If you do not want to create a new
Server Group In              ARCON PAM with this
request if not present.
Note : Do not pass any value in the
"ARCOSServerGroup" parameter if you want to
new server group by using this flag.
And if the value passed in the
"ARCOSServerGroup" parameter is invalid then
it will check the "IsCreateArcosServerGroup" flag
and if it is found to be true then-new a group will
be created.
The default value is "False" if the parameter is not
set.
NewServerGroupN
ame
string Value : New server group name which you want
to create in ARCON.
Please Note this value is mandatory if you set the
"IsCreateArcosServerGroup" value to true.
The default value is "blank" if the parameter is not
set.
CallingApplication
Name
string Value : Name of third party application who is
raising request
Default Value is "ProvisioningAPI" if the
parameter is not set.
UserGroupId string This value refers to Usergroup Id present in
ARCON PAM
Multiple values can be passed seperated
by comma.
Parameter available from ARCON PAM

## [p264]

Type Parameters Data Type Description
OSorDB string This value refers to the Target server type
whether Operating system or Database.
NameOfOSorDB string This value refers to the Name of the target server
type
InstanceName string This value refers to the Name of the database
instance where the user is created
DBName string This value refers to the Database name for the
target device
UserToBeCreated string This value refers to the Username to be created
on the target server
DBRole string This value refers to the Role for user-created on
target
ARCOSFlag string This is used to identify whether the Service needs
to be created in ARCON PAM or Not.
SourceDetails string
HomeDirectory string This value refers to the Directory name for Linux
in case don't want to create a user in the default
home directory.
Port string This value refers to the Port number for Target
Server
Values will be like:
 OS (for the operating system)
 DB (For the database)
Values will be like:
Windows/Linux/Unix/Solaris/Oracle/
SQL/MYSQL
Values will be like:
 "Y" - To create service in ARCON
PAM
 "N" - Not to create service in
ARCON PAM

erGroup

ame

string This value refers to User Organizational Unit on
AD server.

value will be 'false')

Root/admin password policy.
false - New service will be created using
Default Password policy.
Parameter available from ARCOM PAM
Ver 4850-U16.

'0' if not passed.
Parameter available from ARCOM PAM
Ver 4850-U16.
Values will be like : Default value will be
taken from Global config (Default
password age for new service) if not
passed.
Parameter available from ARCOM PAM
Ver 4850-U16.
This Parameter is Mandatory only when
Using value ‘ActiveDirectory' in
'NameOfOSorDB’ parameter above.
OU must be separated by pipe and value
should be passed in reverse order.

Ver 4850 U18.

e

## [p303]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 303
Type Parameters Data Type Description
OSorDB string This value refers to the Target server type
whether Operating system or Database.
NameOfOSorDB string Name of target server type
InstanceName string This value refers to the Name of the database
instance where you want to create a user
DBName string This value refers to the Database name for the
target device
UserToBeCreated string This value refers to the Username to be created
on the target server
DBRole string This value refers to the access or privileges for
user-created on target.
Values will be like:
 OS (for the operating system)
 DB (For the database)
Values will be like:
 Windows/Linux/Unix/Solaris/Oracle/
SQL/MYSQL/ActiveDirectory
Use ActiveDirectory when deleting
Domain User (Available from ARCON
PAM Ver 4.8.5.0 U18)
Values will be like :
SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE or
ALL
Values will be comma seperated.
Available from 4850 U10.

## [p304]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 304
Type Parameters Data Type Description
ARCOSFlag string This is used to identify whether the Service needs
to be created in ARCON PAM or Not.
Port string This value refers to the Port number for Target
Server (Will use default port if not sent)
UniqueId string Currently not implemented
RequesterUsernam
e
string This value refers to the Username who is raising
requests for the assigned group. User should be
present in ARCON PAM
TicketId string This value refers to the Ticket id from service to
track the status
ARCONPAMAction string This value refers to the action to be taken in
ARCON PAM after user deleted on target device
CallingApplication
Name
string This value refers to name of third party
application who is raising request
Values will be like:
 "Y" - To create service in ARCON
PAM
 "N" - Not to create service in
ARCON PAM
Values will be like : 'disable' or 'delete'
Default value is 'disable' if not passed
anything.
delete - will permanently delete service
and supporting
log data from ARCONPAM.
disable - will disable service in ARCON
PAM.
Default Value is "ProvisioningAPI" if
the parameter is not set.

## [p313]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 313
Type Parameters Data Type Description
OSorDB string This value refers to the Target server type
whether Operating system or Database.
NameOfOSorDB string Name of target server type
InstanceName string This value refers to the Name of the database
instance where you want to create a user
DBName string This value refers to the Database name for the
target device
UserToBeCreated string This value refers to the Username to be created
on the target server
DBRole string This value refers to the access or privileges for
user-created on target.
Values will be like:
 OS (for the operating system)
 DB (For the database)
Values will be like:
 Windows/Linux/Unix/Solaris/Oracle/
SQL/MYSQL/ActiveDirectory
Use ActiveDirectory when removing
groups on Domain server (Available
from ARCON PAM Ver 4.8.5.0 U18)
Values will be like :
SELECT,INSERT,UPDATE,DELETE or
ALL
Values will be comma seperated.
Available from 4850 U10.

## [p590]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 590
22 Introduction
ARCON PAM functions to secure privileged accounts in an organization. ARCON PAM APIs automates the
task and provides systematic control over operations including managing users and service accounts. API
Integration provides the necessary framework which links customers ticketing systems like ITESM, BMC
Remedy, Service Now, Manage Engine, Symphony, Arksight, etc to ARCON PAM sessions. The APIs for login
authentication and vault integration will provide holistic security and reduce risk in a company. API is already a
part of the ARCON PAM Installation and therefore can be used without setting any different configurations. All
topics covered in this guide adhere to RESTful standards making it REST APIs.
22.1 Authentication JWT Token Flow
This API call is an authentication mechanism, implemented using OAuth 2.0 JSON Web Tokens bearer flow,
this flow requires prior user registration in ARCON PAM Client Manager (ACMO). The registered user can be
used to generate tokens using the following mentioned API call.
This endpoint is mandatory for consuming any other endpoints. This bearer flow JWT Token generation
requires prior user registration for consuming User-Role based Endpoints.
22.1.1 Reference Documents
1. JSON Web Tokens detailed documentation: https://jwt.io/
2. OAuth 2.0 detailed documentation: https://oauth.net/2/
22.1.2 arconToken - Token Generation By using Refresh Token
This API is used for generating Json Web Token (JWT) Token-based authentication mechanism. It accepts
‘grant_type', ‘refreshToken’, and authenticates the user consuming the API, and in return gives out a JWT
Token along with its refresh token. Each access token is valid for the time value given in 'expires_in’, which is in
milliseconds.
Type of Request POST
Endpoint /arconToken
Available in API
Version
All versions
Release Version U3
Pre Endpoint Call /arconToken
Code samples given, use third-party libraries, as given by 'Postman Rest Client' which are as follows:
1. For C# using Rest-Sharp, https://www.nuget.org/packages/RestSharp/105.2.3
2. For Java using OK HTTP: https://square.github.io/okhttp/
3. For Python
a. Using HTTP client: https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.client.html
b. Using requests: https://pypi.org/project/requests/
ARCON does not take any responsibility for any bugs/vulnerabilities in the third-party libraries
neither does ARCON recommend usage for these third-party libraries. Similar code can be done in
native languages respectively for achieving the same results.

22.1.2.1 Data Types of Request and Response
Type Parameters Data Type Description
Request grant_type string This is usually a string value, currently supported
values are ‘password’ & ' refresh_token', as described
in detail below:
There are multiple grant_types which are
supported in OAuth 2.0, but currently, we
only support the following 2 grant_types
 password : This is grant_type, which is
supported, and it requires username
and password as mandatory inputs
along with grant_type as Password.
 refresh_token: This requires
refresh_token from the previous
request to generate another token and
refresh_token. This does not require a
username and password.

## [p592]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 592
Type Parameters Data Type Description
refresh_token string refresh_token value from the previous call for
generating a token, based on which there will be a
new pair or access_token and refresh_token will be
generated.
Response access_token string Token value, which is a long, encrypted string value.
This value can be divided into 3 parts, header,
payload, and signature. This Token is to pass into the
header of every PAM API to be consumed
henceforth, till the time it expires.
token_type string ‘Bearer’
expires_in int Value is in milliseconds
refresh_token string Token value, which is a long, encrypted string value.
This value can be divided into 3 parts, header,
payload, and signature. After the ‘access_token’ is
expired, this Token used to generate new
‘access_token’ and ‘refresh_token’ without using
‘username’ and ‘password’. This is preferable for the
robotic process, to consume API’s.

22.2 SIEM
Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) provides real-time analysis of security alerts generated by
network hardware and applications. SIEM solutions are used to log security data and generate reports for
compliance purposes.
22.2.1 GetUserLoginAttempt
This API provides information related to login attempts made by the User, in the specified period of the
timeline given as input in fields of ‘FromDate’ and ‘ToDate’.
Type of Request POST
Endpoint /api/SIEM/GetUserLoginAttempt
Available in API
Version
All versions
Release Version U13
Pre Endpoint Call /arconToken
Request Params - - - -
Headers Content-Type application/x-www-
form-urlencoded
Mandatory -
Authorization bearer eyJ0[...
Removed for
brevity ....]q0gs
x-PAM-Version - Not Applicable -
Body
{
    "FromDate": "2019-06-22T02:37:00",
    "ToDate": "2019-06-26T12:37:00",
    "NumberOfRecords": 2
}
The refresh_token authentication bearer token flow involves the following:
1. First time /arconToken has to be consumed using ‘username' and ‘password' are always in
base64 encoded format, then onwards, the ‘refresh_token’ can be used in /arconToken to
generate new 'access_token' and 'refresh_token’, henceforth.
2. The 'grant_type' is always 'password' for generating the JWT Token.
3. Code samples given are generated by Postman Rest Client, they need packages for various
namespaces or objects of classes to be usable, please import the same before using it.

22.3 Service Details
A service is an instance of a server. In ARCON PAM, the routers, firewalls, switches, and databases are some of
the services created to connect to the target server. These services need to be mapped to users.  The users
mapped to the services will have the privilege to connect to the target server using these services.
For example, Suppose there are four users Admin, Client, TEST, and UAT on a windows server. Each user may
have a unique requirement of service to perform on the server. Hence, the Administrator will create services
for each of the users. These services are then grouped and mapped to each of the users which helps the
Administrator to manage the services which are mapped to the user. Thereby, also helping the Administrator in
user wise audit trail performed in ARCON PAM.

Type Parameters Data Type Description
Password string This value refers to the password of the ARCON
user
DomainName string This value refers to the domain of the ARCON
user
IPAddress string This value refers to IP address from which the
user logged in to ARCON
IPMacAddress string This value refers to mac address from which the
user logged in to ARCON
ConnectionType string This value refers to the what type of connection
user taken, (AG,ACMOCLI,SSO)
ProcessorID string This value refers to the processor id of the
ARCON user
BIOSSerialID string This value refers to the BIOSSerialID of the
ARCON user
Response Message string This value refers to a success or failure message
If user is authenticated, result field would contain
the userid
If user is not authenticated, Error message would
be
“ Invalid User Name OR Password,Authent
ication Failed ”

22.3.44 RaisingServiceAccessRequest
This API is used to raise service access for Permanent, One-time, and Time-Based requests, without workflow
in ARCON PAM. If the workflow is present in the client environment, then this API will not be useful and throw
out errors, stating that it cannot process as the Workflow is in place. The one-time and time-based service
access request behave in a similar fashion to that of Just-in-time based requests.
Type of Request POST

22.4 User Details
A User is an entity that has the authority to use an application. Users shall be of two types such as Client User
and Admin User. The Client type of User shall be responsible only for checking reports and accessing services.
The Client User will not have admin privileges to perform any admin activity in Server Manager whereas the
Admin User shall be able to perform all the activities in ARCON PAM.
While Logging into ARCON PAM, the Admin/Client type of User shall select the respective domains (AD
Domain/ Local Domain) for authentication. The Users authenticated from Active Directory shall be called
Domain Users whereas, the Users authenticated from local Domain are known as Local User.

## [p1125]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 1125
 Domain User: A domain user is a user whose username and password are stored on a domain controller
rather than the computer through which the User is logging into. When you log in as a Domain User, the
computer asks the domain controller what privileges are assigned to you. When the computer receives
an appropriate response from the domain controller, it logs you in with the permissions and restrictions.
 Local User:   A local User is one whose username and encrypted password are stored on the computer
itself. When you log in as a local user, the computer checks its own list of Users and its own password file
to see if you are allowed to log into the standalone computer.
22.4.1 UserDetailsV2
A User is an entity that has the authority to use an application. Users shall be of two types such as Client User
and Admin User. The Client type of User shall be responsible only for checking reports and accessing services.
The Client User will not have admin privileges to perform any admin activity in Server Manager whereas the
Admin User shall be able to perform all the activities in ARCON PAM.
While Logging into ARCON PAM, the Admin/Client type of User shall select the respective domains (AD
Domain/ Local Domain) for authentication. The Users authenticated from Active Directory shall be called
Domain Users whereas, the Users authenticated from local Domain are known as Local User.
 Domain User: A domain user is a user whose username and password are stored on a domain controller
rather than the computer through which the User is logging into. When you log in as a Domain User, the
computer asks the domain controller what privileges are assigned to you. When the computer receives
an appropriate response from the domain controller, it logs you in with the permissions and restrictions.
 Local User:   A local User is one whose username and encrypted password are stored on the computer
itself. When you log in as a local user, the computer checks its own list of Users and its own password file
to see if you are allowed to log into the standalone computer.

22.4.1.4.1 Data Types of Request and Response
Type Parameters Data Type Description
Request UserId int This value refers to the id of the user present in
ARCON PAM
Response ServiceId int This value refers to the id of the service assigned
to the ARCON PAM user
IPAddress string This value refers to the IP address of the service
present in ARCON PAM
HostName string This value refers to the hostname of the service
present in ARCON PAM
ServiceUserName string This value is in encrypted format refers to the
username of the service present in ARCON PAM
Port int This value refers to the port of the service present
in ARCON PAM
ServiceType string This value refers to the type of service present in
ARCON PAM
ServiceDomain string This value refers to the domain of the service
present in ARCON PAM
Mandatory Parameter.

22.4.2 UserDetailsV3
A User is an entity that has the authority to use an application. Users shall be of two types such as Client User
and Admin User. The Client type of User shall be responsible only for checking reports and accessing services.
The Client User will not have admin privileges to perform any admin activity in Server Manager whereas the
Admin User shall be able to perform all the activities in ARCON PAM.
While Logging into ARCON PAM, the Admin/Client type of User shall select the respective domains (AD
Domain/ Local Domain) for authentication. The Users authenticated from Active Directory shall be called
Domain Users whereas, the Users authenticated from local Domain are known as Local User.
 Domain User: A domain user is a user whose username and password are stored on a domain controller
rather than the computer through which the user is logging into. When you log in as a Domain User, the
computer asks the domain controller what privileges are assigned to you. When the computer receives
an appropriate response from the domain controller, it logs you in with the permissions and restrictions.

## [p1207]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 1207
 Local User:   A local User is one whose username and encrypted password are stored on the computer
itself. When you log in as a local user, the computer checks its own list of Users and its own password file
to see if you are allowed to log into the standalone computer.

DBInstanceName string This value refers to the instance of the service
present in ARCON PAM

Description1 string This value refers to the description 1 specify to
that service

that service

that service

22.7 Configuration
This is to fetch ARCOS configuration details to enable real time session monitoring from the database.
Configuration details entered by the user are stored in ARCOS database, these API’s can be called to retrieve
the configuration details from the table.
22.7.1 DecryptText
This API is used to decrypt AES encrypted text .The Key is first 32 character of the token by which the text is
encrypted .If encrypted text and key both are correct ,then only it will decrypt ,otherwise validation error
“Entered Encrypted Text is either not correct or key is not valid”
Type of Request POST
Endpoint api/Configuration/DecryptText

22.8 ServicePassword
Mismanagement of Privileged Users and their passwords is a major cause of security breaches and one of the
top reasons for passwords unavailability that leads to a long recovery processes from IT failures. Password
Management helps a user to store and organize passwords.  The password vault is an electronic vault, which
stores the privileged passwords in a highly secured manner. The vault is AES-256 bit encrypted, which is
further wrapped with a proprietary encryption algorithm. The electronic vault requires authorization of users
for secured printing. The password vault secures all the passwords with its proprietary encryption
methodology. Further, it also provides dynamic password generation facility.

22.9 ADbridging
Before consuming APIs in the ADbridging section, a JWT Token must be generated and passed in the header
for all APIs given below.
Code samples given use third-party libraries, as given by 'Postman Rest Client' which are as follows:
1. For C# using Rest-Sharp, https://www.nuget.org/packages/RestSharp/105.2.3
2. For Java using OK HTTP: https://square.github.io/okhttp/
3. For Python
a. Using HTTP client: https://docs.python.org/3/library/http.client.html
b. Using requests: https://pypi.org/project/requests/
ARCON does not take any responsibility for any bugs/vulnerabilities in the third-party libraries
neither does ARCON recommend usage for these third-party libraries. Similar code can be done in
native languages respectively for achieving the same results.

access logs
AccessType string This value refers to the access type of the service

CurrentStatus string This value refers to the current status of the
service access
PendingWith string This value refers to the username of the ARCON
PAM user by which approval is pending
FinalApprover string This value refers to the username of the ARCON
PAM user which is the final approver
WFID long This value refers to the id of the service access

## [p2106]

www.arconnet.com|Copyright © 2026 2106
36 RTSM
RTSM is Real Time Session Monitoring. Administrative users require privileged account access in their day-to-
day roles to maintain systems, perform upgrades and troubleshoot issues. However, these users can also
misuse their privileges to gain unauthorized access to sensitive information or cause damage to the IT
environment. To deter the misuse of privileges by authorized users, as well as detect malicious activity,
organizations should proactively record and monitor all privileged session activity.
Real Time Session Monitoring monitors the live feed of a session. You can quickly freeze, unfreeze or logout the
session to minimize any potential damage. It increases the control over user's activity.

37 ServiceCreation
37.1 Overview
A service represents a specific access point or connection type to a target server. In ARCON | Privileged Access
Management (PAM), components such as routers, firewalls, switches, and databases are configured as services
to facilitate secure connections to target systems.
These services must be mapped to users to grant access. Only users assigned to a service are authorized to
connect to the corresponding target server through that service.
The Service Creation module enables administrators to define and manage these services efficiently.

38 ServicePassword - DRAFT - Do not use
38.1 Overview
Mismanagement of Privileged Users and their passwords is a major cause of security breaches and one of the
top reasons for passwords unavailability that leads to a long recovery process from IT failures.
Password Management helps a user to store and organize passwords. The password vault is an electronic vault,
which stores the privileged passwords in a highly secured manner. The vault is AES-256 bit encrypted, which is
further wrapped with a proprietary encryption algorithm. The electronic vault requires authorization of users
for secured printing. The password vault secures all the passwords with its proprietary encryption
methodology. Further, it also provides dynamic password generation facility..

41.1.1 Data Types of Request and Response

user
Response Id int This value refers to the id of the LOB present in
ARCON PAM
Name string This value refers to the name of the LOB present
in ARCON PAM

inactive
AccessType string This value refers to the access type by which API
user can be accessed
AccessRowIds int This value refers to row id of the API user details

UserSecret string This value refers to the user secret of the API user
UserKey string This value refers to the user key of the API user
CreatedByUserId int This value refers to the id by which API user-
created
UpdatedByUserId int This value refers to the id by which API user
details are updated
